body.statement: Supporting corollary (Howard et al. and Ville inversion): for every predictable policy and every mean vector \(\mu=(\mu_j)_{j\in\mathcal J}\), \(\mathbb P_\mu\{\mu_j\geq B_{j,s}\text{ for all }j\in\mathcal J\text{ and }0\leq s\leq n\}\geq1-\alpha\). If \(N_{j,s}=0\), then \(B_{j,s}=-\infty\).
body.justification: This cited Ville-inversion corollary supplies simultaneous reporting alongside the optimized design; it is not a novelty-bearing result.
body.gap: Howard et al. provide time-uniform supermartingale inversion; subgroupwise allocation of error and a union bound give this direct supporting corollary, including the zero-information endpoint.
body.consumer: Trial reports obtain simultaneous one-sided effect sequences even when the optimal policy stops sampling a subgroup.
